open_obligations: Check whether the strength of easy-to-hard generalization differs across Hase et al.'s datasets and between Sun et al.'s generators and evaluators.
Check difficulty gaps: grade levels versus MATH levels.
Do not combine Hase et al.'s relative results with Sun et al.'s absolute MATH500 scores.
in.other_title: Easy-to-hard generalization: reward models trained on easy problems supervise hard ones
in.rationale: Hase et al. report LMs finetuned or prompted with easy data often do nearly as well on hard data as with hard data. Sun et al. report reward models trained on easy problems (e.g. levels 1-3) can supervise generators on hard problems via re-ranking or RL; Hase et al. study generators directly via ICL, probes and QLoRA, Sun et al. study evaluators, so results should not be transferred between them.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether supervision on easy problems suffices for good performance on hard problems

text: The paper presents the surprising conclusion that current pretrained language models often generalize relatively well from easy to hard data, even performing as well as oracle models finetuned on hard data, using in-context learning, linear classifier heads and QLoRA across seven hardness measures (six human, one loss-based). It also argues that, since hard data is generally noisier and costlier to collect, collecting easy data can be better even for hard-test performance.
title: Easy-to-hard generalization: LMs often generalize relatively well from easy to hard data
